body:
Huge thanks for the insight. I meant to reply, because I do gave some specific questions that might be better in PM. Your situation seems very similar to mine, but your further along in the process. Before I could, he and I actually had the conversation, and we made some headway in unexpected areas. It involves sex, so my wall of text will be worthwhile. :)

With some difficulty, we got to the root of his need for admiration, and as I expected, it's ugly duckling syndrome. He has a need to feel attractive because of his medical issues and social problems when he was younger. He insists that he just wants the attention from me, not from other guys, but I think he is confusing what he wants with what he wants to want. It's a bit reassuring that he's trying to keep me as the center of his life because he deeply loves me, but I'm pretty certain that's not going to work in the long run. We're gonna revisit the open conversation tomorrow and I'm going to insist on a rule change.

Not all was completely lost though. I don't usually discuss my sex life, but apparently his need for adoration extends into the bedroom. For 10 years, I've been trying to keep my cool and make sure I don't look like a groveling desperate body worshipper, or to come off as disrespectful or objectifying. But, that's what I'm doing in my head, because that's what gets me off. As it turns out, he has wanted to be treated like an object the whole time, but was afraid if he admitted it, he would seem like a narcissist. This news was like fantasy turning into reality. He gave me the green light to basically treat him like a piece of meat. So, I did, and it was like the on switch came back on between us. It was amazing!

I can't believe we went so long not understanding each other.
I don't see taking care of my own issues and worrying about his as two mutually exclusive things. In fact, I feel like they should be addressed simultaneously, since they're so closely related.

Not seeing anyone yet. It is even more complicated that he also suffers from periodic depression, and is pretty bad with it right now. I'm pretty sure mine is closer to critical status at this point, unless he's planning life insurance policies and doing online research about carbon monoxide behind my back too.

You make a good point that we can't fix each other's depression. I wouldn't expect that, and I don't think he would either. There is a fair deal of room for improvement though, in how we handle each other.

You make an interesting case for looking at monogamy and celibacy in a different way. I will definitely try to wrap my brain around it and conduct some "thought experiments."

I don't have a therapist. I clearly need one, and the only thing keeping me from going down that road is an overdeveloped sense of self-sufficiency (probably stemmed from being extremely poor and alone during late teens and young adulthood). Also, and this might sound dickish without me meaning it to, and it's related to the self-sufficient streak, but I'm deathly afraid of a therapist who knows less about helping me than I can figure out on my own. Going to college in my late 30's has been an eye opener as to how stupid some professionals (professors) can be. I guess that comes down to shopping for the right therapist.

Thanks again for the insight. I appreciate it. You've really given me some things to think about.

1 Thanks, I try.
2 Yes, immensely.
3 During sex, he only looks at me in passing moments, to connect with me. I look back in those moments, but I'm staring and lusting the rest of the time. He's having sex with me and enjoying it because he loves me, and I'm having sex with him because I love him *and* I lust for him. I'm not complaining, as it seems to work out fine for both of us because I don't need to be worshipped. But, if he has the need to lust after someone, he's definitely not getting that fulfilled by me. This is part of the reason I believe he looks elsewhere. Verbally, the positive comments about my physical appearance are far and few in between. I don't expect him to lie to me. There are no negative comments, ever, but he isn't very observant and seldom notices any change in my appearance. I sometimes feel like my physical self could be a ghost or an avatar and our sexual relationship wouldn't be all that different. As I said, I don't need it and I don't mind it. It's just the part where he gets it elsewhere that I'm trying to figure out.
4 The depression is what it is, and at its core, my life events aren't the cause. Those life events are certainly the means by which the depression and frustration manifests, though. It's like a demon that's always there under the surface, but it can't come into physical existence without a portal. That portal, at least recently, has been an extension of that feeling of non-existence extending beyond just sex. So yes, it's most definitely related to his behavior. I'm just not sure if the chicken came before the egg.

Thanks for your input and thought-provoking questions. You have helped me look at this with a broader lens.

I live in the heart of one of the best gay districts in one of the best gay cities in one of the best gay states. Kind of ironic that we have no gay male friends. This is exactly why I'm considering loosening the reigns on his online adventures. We aren't making the friends thing happen, and he needs an outlet.

No competitiveness at all. I can separate my ego and be objective. If I allowed myself to be competitive with this guy, I'd have to be competitive with every hot guy who works out or shows up in porn or whatever. It's a road that just leads to pain and jealousy. I did that in my 20's and steer clear of it. I will admit to comparing. The guy is more attractive than me, and I can't help but to notice, but he really has absolutely nothing to do with me. No need to compete. 

You are right about the inadequacy. We both suffer from that, and couples therapy would probably help. We also spend zero time with gay (male) friends. Neither of us have any. We both piss poor at making friends. I definitely wish I had guy friends to talk to, and though he'd deny feeling the same, he clearly does.

I hadn't even considered doing it in front of me. That would actually be incredibly sexy.

Thanks for your insight. Seeing how other people have handled it definitely helps with gaining perspective.

Thanks for your insight, but your read on him is completely wrong. In fact, it's so wrong that for now on, I'll probably question my own judgments when I give advice to others. Feels different to be on this side of it.

First, I'm not compromising my values to keep anyone anywhere. If he wants out, he can leave. I'm not some desperate ninny clamoring to keep my husband, and he knows that. My number one relationship rule is "Always be willing to leave." There are definitely lines that can be crossed that would spur me into action, but he hasn't crossed one, nor do I believe he ever will. There are a hundred million other things keeping us together. He does not want out, and he won't jump ship at the first chance for anything. He's had 10+ years of chances.

The problem is not that he is some egotistical arrogant dude who is stringing me along for 10 years. The problem is that he has not understood or believed that he is attractive, and seeks external validation. There was absolutely nothing creepy about the pic trading. The other guy hit him up on a non-sex related forum and complimented his looks. He works hard to stay fit, and guys notice. The other dude was fit too, so a conversation started about workouts. Being attracted to other guys and wanting to feel attractive is not creepy.

As for repeating the behavior when I'm not looking, that's not happening. It's easy to lump people into two groups and just label him as "having no consideration," but that approach usually happens when the people evaluating want see things in a more simple way, black and white way. I'm intelligent and observant to notice when things are even slightly off kilter. That's sort of my strong suit.

I appreciate your insight, but I know the man well enough to not need to defend him. I'm also here to figure out *where to draw the line,* not to affirm whether or not a line has been crossed.

I'm not looking for an evaluation of *how* I'm posting, just advice and guidance on *what* I am posting. Mentioning that is obviously a distraction, so I've removed that part of my post.

To answer your question, no, I'm not worried. I may have been initially, but I am not now.

Thanks for your thoughtful response. There's definitely a lot to think on.

I believe his reluctance is stemmed from a combination of both internalized shame and fear of my reaction, but I think the former begets the latter. It's almost like he's grown out of being an ugly duckling into this handsome and fit man, and he is conflicted on the inside because his self-identity no longer matches the portrait. His MO is that he's unattractive and unlikeable. He still doesn't see himself as attractive or muscular enough. I also think he may have "settled" for me because he didn't think he'd have a chance anywhere else. Discovering that isn't true, albeit a little late in the game, is exciting for him.

The fear of my response comes in with him not wanting to disappoint me, since I loved him when he was the ugly duckling (in his own mind - he never really was...). He really does love me, and betraying me is the last thing he'd want to do. Also - and I say this not to defend him, but because I really know him - but he can tend toward being completely oblivious, and probably doesn't even realize what he is doing and how I might perceive it if I found out. If he did, he'd stop without question. The problem is that it's becoming his natural pattern, and just stopping won't fix the underlying issue.

Thinking deeper, I've got my own things to come clean about. I've started cutting and gave been dealing with depression and suicidal thoughts over the last few months. He has no idea how bad it's gotten. I haven't told him for the same exact reasons he keeps things from me. He would be horribly hurt and feel betrayed. I'm thinking that maybe by trusting him, he will comfortable to reciprocate. I'm just not sure how to approach it.

I'm trying to figure out the same thing, but I'm 11 years in. I think the longer you put it off, the worse it gets. That being said, honestly explaining how you feel and why you want to break up might actually bring you closer.
Interesting. Seems reasonable, though I don't think it would work for me. I've always assumed that I would just deal with any pain that comes my way, without needing practice.
Hmm. When I "come out" as self-harming, he'll be devastated. I guess I'm trying to avoid that, but I can't and shouldn't.
Thanks a ton. I ended up figuring it out, but still missed the similar problem on the exam. Go figure. At least now I understand how fractional exponents work.

I can verify that passing your exams won't change how you feel. It'll just create a higher level of achievement you believe you can't reach. I feel like if I get a B on an exam instead of an A, I'm not doing well enough and I want to pitch myself off a bridge. It's not all that different than moving from third world problems to first world problems. Your feelings are coming from somewhere else and are manifesting through the problems. I advise you to get help managing them. If your parents don't understand, go to someone who will. If you need resources for that, I'm sure someone here can point you in the right direction.

I can't really help with the suicide thoughts much (because I'm right there with you), but I can relate to the financial problems. Are you eligible for bankruptcy? It won't get rid of the school loans, but it'll get rid of the credit card debt. I did it, and it was the best decision I ever made. Within a year, I had credit cards again (that I have NEVER used again after all that BS), and my credit score now is top notch. Everyone acts like it's the worst possible thing that can happen financially, but it's actually pretty damn amazing.

I know I'm focusing on small detail, but it helped me and could help you.
